name: Genetic Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy

criteria.description: Persistent, severe watery diarrhea starting in the neonatal period or early infancy
Exclusion of infectious, allergic, and metabolic causes of diarrhea
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes associated with congenital diarrheal disorders
Evidence of malabsorption including failure to thrive and electrolyte imbalances
Intestinal biopsy showing villous atrophy or epithelial abnormalities consistent with genetic diarrhea

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent severe diarrhea starting in infancy with exclusion of other causes plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including genetic testing and intestinal biopsy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe watery diarrhea refractory to dietary changes
searchTerms: severe watery diarrhea not helped by diet
persistent watery stools despite dietary changes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Onset of diarrhea within first weeks of life
searchTerms: diarrhea starting in first weeks of life
infantile diarrhea beginning soon after birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to malabsorption
searchTerms: poor growth from nutrient absorption problems
not gaining weight due to digestion issues
electrolyte problems like low potassium and acid-base imbalance
abnormal blood minerals and metabolic acidosis

laboratory: Malabsorption markers (low serum albumin, vitamin deficiencies)
Stool studies showing high volume watery diarrhea without infectious agents
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show bowel wall thickening
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes such as EPCAM, MYO5B, or other congenital diarrheal disorder genes
other: Intestinal biopsy showing villous atrophy, epithelial abnormalities, or tufting enteropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset compared to genetic intractable diarrhea
Characteristic microvillus inclusions on electron microscopy
Severe neonatal diarrhea with similar presentation but distinct histopathology

redFlags: Failure to thrive despite nutritional interventions
references: Orphanet: Genetic Intractable Diarrhea of Infancy - ORPHA:363300
